name: Brunei
summary: A small, oil-rich sultanate on Borneo, a British protectorate from 1888 and fully independent in 1984.

location.value: The north-west coast of Borneo, in two parts split by the Malaysian state of Sarawak; about 5,765 km².

terrain.value: A low coastal plain with rivers and swamps; tropical rainforest in the hills, especially in Temburong district.

climate.value: Equatorial: hot and humid all year, with heavy rain especially from about October to January.

resources.value: Oil (found at Seria in 1929) and natural gas, both onshore and offshore; also rainforest timber.

disasters.value: Floods and landslides in heavy rain; smoke haze from forest fires elsewhere in Borneo, as in 1997–98.

population.value: About 450,000–460,000 people in the mid-2020s, including many foreign workers.

urbanisation.value: Most people live in towns; the capital Bandar Seri Begawan includes the water village Kampong Ayer, and Seria and Kuala Belait are oil towns.

disease.value: Free public health care for citizens; lifestyle illnesses such as diabetes and heart disease are major concerns.

migration.value: Many foreign workers from Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia and South Asia work in building, services and homes.

economicBase.value: Oil and gas provide most export income and government revenue, mainly through Brunei Shell Petroleum and LNG exports.

tradeRoutes.value: Liquefied natural gas and crude oil shipped mainly to Japan, South Korea and other Asian buyers.

wealth.value: A high-income economy thanks to oil and gas, with a large sovereign wealth fund, the Brunei Investment Agency.

moneyAndTax.value: The Brunei dollar, kept equal in value to the Singapore dollar; there is no personal income tax.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: An absolute monarchy: the sultan is head of state and prime minister, and rules by decree.

keyRulers.value: Omar Ali Saifuddien III. Hassanal Bolkiah.

succession.value: Hereditary within the royal family that has ruled Brunei for centuries; the sultan names the crown prince.

institutions.value: The Council of Cabinet Ministers, Privy Council and Religious Council, and an appointed Legislative Council restored in 2004.

stability.value: Stable since independence in 1984; emergency powers first declared after the 1962 revolt are still renewed.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: The small Royal Brunei Armed Forces, plus a British Army Gurkha battalion based at Seria under a defence agreement.

majorWars.value: No wars since independence in 1984; the last fighting was the brief 1962 revolt, before independence.

territoryChange.value: No changes since independence; Brunei had chosen not to join Malaysia in 1963 and claims part of the South China Sea.

alliancesRivals.value: Joined ASEAN and the United Nations in 1984; also a member of the Commonwealth and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: Free education for citizens; Universiti Brunei Darussalam was founded in 1985, followed by other universities.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Good roads, the Temburong Bridge (2020) joining the two parts, Brunei International Airport and Muara port.

religion.value: Islam (Sunni, Shafi’i) is the state religion followed by most people, with Christian and Buddhist minorities.

languageWriting.value: Malay is the official language, written in Latin and Jawi script; English is widely used in business and education.

artsArchitecture.value: Grand mosques such as the Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque (1958), stilt houses of Kampong Ayer, and brass and silver crafts.

socialStructure.value: A Malay majority, a Chinese minority, Indigenous groups such as the Dusun and Murut, and many foreign workers.

sharedIdentity.value: The official ideology of Melayu Islam Beraja (Malay Islamic Monarchy), proclaimed at independence in 1984.

dailyLife.value: Comfortable town life for most citizens; foods include ambuyat (sago starch) and nasi katok rice packs.

neighbours.value: Malaysia (the state of Sarawak), which surrounds Brunei on land, and the South China Sea to the north.

ideasReligions.value: A strongly Islamic state; it began bringing in a Sharia penal code in stages from 2014.

peakPeriod.value: Too recent to judge; oil wealth since independence in 1984 has kept living standards high.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Still in existence as an independent sultanate and member of ASEAN and the United Nations.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
